# GameSpot — prerelease gameplay preview

- Original source: [GameSpot — prerelease gameplay preview](https://www.gamespot.com/articles/robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood-preview/1100-2895665/)
- Author / publication: Elliott Chin / GameSpot
- Language / date: English; 2002 prerelease coverage
- Access: Live page blocked (HTTP 403); text read from the Wayback Machine capture
- Checked: 2026-09-09
- Retrieved: 2026-09-09, from the 2015-03-16 capture
- Archived copy: [Wayback Machine, 2015-03-16](https://web.archive.org/web/20150316044844/http://www.gamespot.com/articles/robin-hood-the-legend-of-sherwood-preview/1100-2895665/)
- Format: header notes, original summary, then complete factual notes (commercial article, not transcribed)

A detailed preview of the campaign loop: early introductory missions lead to Sherwood, where the player assigns production and training before selecting further operations. It discusses the tradeoff between taking strong characters into the field and leaving them to develop at camp.

The article describes beggars revealing information through map scrolls, patrols investigating disturbances, and guards reviving or freeing disabled comrades. It also contrasts short forest ambushes with more involved castle missions.

**Accuracy caution:** this is prerelease reporting. It places Stuteley's rescue in Leicester and makes restrictive claims about which characters can perform certain abilities; these should be checked against the released game rather than copied into a specification.

**Research use:** contemporary descriptions of design intentions and how the strategic layer was presented before launch.

## Detailed notes

Page facts: "Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood Preview", subtitle likens it to "the prince of thieves meets Commandos 2", by Elliott Chin, 24 October 2002, published by Strategy First. Commercial article, so paraphrased.

- Story setup as told: Robin returns from the Crusades declared dead so the sheriff could take his land; critics of the sheriff, including his family, imprisoned or killed. Mission 1: break into the castle of a family friend, itself confiscated by the sheriff. Mission 2: free the outlaw Stutely and his men from the stocks, placed by the preview in "the town of Leicester" (the released game uses Nottingham). Stutely then invites Robin to Sherwood.
- Structure: two forced prologue missions, then a free-form map of Sherwood and surroundings with missions appearing at trade routes and castles; sometimes only one mission is offered, but the feel is one of choice.
- Resource layer: abilities like nets and arrows consume finite items; men left in Sherwood craft arrows, sew purses and nets, harvest herbs, pick apples, hunt meat, rest, and train sword and archery; output reported on return and scales with the number assigned; the tradeoff of taking your best men versus leaving them to train.
- Locations: five castles and three countryside intersections, revisited across dozens of missions. Ambushes are short and small (get in, grab the money, leave) and read as filler to amass gold and recruit; castle missions carry the story and look overwhelming at first, demanding stealth and piecemeal takedowns.
- Beggars: paying them spawns scrolls at the places you must reach; scrolls sit deep inside castles and usually point to the next beggar.
- Guard behaviour observed: investigate strangers in their line of sight, flee to fetch help when outnumbered, wake and free bound comrades, respond to frightened townsfolk and to children who recognise Robin. Only one Merry Man can carry bodies; others tie or kill unconscious guards; killing hurts reputation and recruitment.
- Party: up to five per mission; Marian sometimes joins but does not live in Sherwood; one mission stops her marriage to Guy of Guisborne. Will Scarlet is rescued from Leicester's dungeons, Little John saved during an ambush-type mission. Generic archetypes: healer (the only one able to kill unconscious men), lummox (only carrier), archer (ties up).
- Abilities as reported: Robin shoots, and is called the only character who punches knockouts and throws purses; purses make groups fight for coins. Stutely: net, apples, beggar disguise, tie up; nets are undone by other guards; apples judged weak. Will Scarlet: sling stone knockout at range, stones only found on maps, plus strangling. Marian: bow, herbs, and a "spy" ability to sense rooms by listening. Healer: apples, herbs, kill sleepers. Archer: tie, bow, shield. Lummox: carry.
- Closing: game looked stable, no crashes during the preview.
